item.text:
**4B.8 Research Note**

Bottom line: **No.** I found no credible 2024 evidence that Khamenei respected succession constraints in a way that made power genuinely transferable. The only positive material is procedural continuity, not real compliance: elections and the Assembly of Experts still existed on paper. The substantive 2024 record is one of hardline vetting, exclusion of plausible alternatives, and blocking oversight bodies that could influence succession.

| Title | Publisher | Date | URL | Claim-level summary | QIDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|
| Iranians expected to shun first election since death of Mahsa Amini | The Guardian | 2024-03-01 | https://www.theguardian.com/world/2024/mar/01/iran-election-expected-turnout-mahsa-amini | The article notes that Iran still held elections for parliament and the 88-seat Assembly of Experts, the body that would choose Khamenei’s successor. That is the closest positive signal I found, but it shows only the existence of formal succession machinery, not that Khamenei respected constraints on it. | 4B.8, 4B.1 |
| Iran bars Hassan Rouhani from seeking re-election to key body | The Guardian | 2024-01-25 | https://www.theguardian.com/world/2024/jan/25/iran-bars-hassan-rouhani-from-seeking-re-election-to-key-body | The Guardian Council blocked Rouhani from the Assembly of Experts, which is charged with appointing the supreme leader and can in theory dismiss him. That is direct evidence against respect for constitutional transfer rules and against an open succession process. | 4B.8, 4B.4, 4B.2 |
| Iran vote turnout hits historic low amid discontent | Reuters via ThePrint | 2024-03-02 | https://www.theprint.in/world/iran-vote-turnout-hits-historic-low-amid-discontent/1986385/ | Reuters described the parliamentary vote and Assembly of Experts election as a legitimacy test under tight restrictions, with turnout around 41 percent. This supports the view that the succession-linked institutions were still tightly managed rather than genuinely open. | 4B.8, 4B.1, 4B.2 |
| Iran election: turnout sinks to record low as polls close | The Guardian | 2024-03-02 | https://www.theguardian.com/world/2024/mar/01/iran-election-expected-turnout-mahsa-amini | The Guardian said many reformists were disqualified and that the new parliament and Assembly of Experts were likely to remain in conservative hands. Some lesser-known provincial candidates did get in, which is a weak procedural counter-signal, but it does not show meaningful respect for transfer constraints. | 4B.8, 4B.1, 4B.2 |
| Iran’s presidential election dominated by Khamenei loyalists | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-06-25 | https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/irans-presidential-election-dominated-by-khamenei-loyalists-3494879 | Reuters said Khamenei ensured hardline candidates dominated the race and that the Guardian Council approved only five hardliners and one low-profile moderate from 80 applicants. That is strong evidence of succession-adjacent rule management and loyalty filtering, not respect for constitutional transfer norms. | 4B.8, 4B.1, 4B.2, 4B.5 |
| Factbox-Iran’s presidential election process | Reuters via KELO-AM | 2024-06-25 | https://kelo.com/2024/06/25/factbox-irans-presidential-election-process/ | Reuters explained that candidates for parliament and the Assembly of Experts must pass Guardian Council vetting, and that half of the Council is appointed by the supreme leader. This is structural evidence that the succession environment remained subordinated to Khamenei’s camp. | 4B.8, 4B.2, 4B.4 |

**Search gap**
- I found no 2024 source showing Khamenei voluntarily accepted a meaningful transfer of power, loosened succession vetting, or honored coalition commitments that would constrain succession outcomes.
- The evidence is overwhelmingly about **managed succession**, not constitutional restraint. The only positive sign is that the formal institutions still existed and elections were held on schedule; that is not the same as respecting them.
